cards.title: max() and min()
cards.body: `max(nums)` gives the largest value in a list and `min(nums)` the smallest.

hi.title: max() aur min()
hi.body: `max(nums)` list ki sabse badi value deta hai aur `min(nums)` sabse chhoti.

cards.title: len() counts items
cards.body: `len(nums)` tells you how many items a list has.

hi.title: len() items ginta hai
hi.body: `len(nums)` batata hai ki list mein kitne items hain.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print how many names are in the list, 3, but prints 4. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: `len(names[0])` counts the letters in the first name. Count the list itself: `len(names)`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse print karna chahiye ki list mein kitne naam hain, yaani 3, par yeh 4 print karta hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: `len(names[0])` pehle naam ke letters ginta hai. List ko hi gino: `len(names)`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Among negative numbers, the one closest to zero is the largest.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Negative numbers mein jo zero ke sabse paas hai, wahi sabse bada hai.

exercise.prompt: Read whole numbers on one line, separated by spaces, and print the largest. Try `max()`.
exercise.promptHi: Ek line mein spaces se alag kiye whole numbers padho aur sabse bada print karo. `max()` try karo.
